known_cyclic_or_abelian_DM7_for_n.note: CPro1 lists CFR(6,21) as open: 'OPEN_INSTANCES = [[6,21],[5,25],[5,27],[4,33]]' (file committed 2025-01-28, unchanged at repository HEAD 827f02b, 2026-06-03). None of the three CPro1 papers solved it, and the repository's designs/ folder has no circular Florentine results. Groups of order 21 are Z_21 and Z_7⋊Z_3; no 7-row difference matrix found over either.
Groups of order 39 are Z_39 and Z_13⋊Z_3; no 7-row difference matrix found over either.
Only the cyclic group has order 51.

known_cyclic_or_abelian_DM7_for_n.context: Nearby difference matrices with 7 or more rows do exist: (Z_35,7;1) in Sym2026; (Z_55,7;1) in Sage DM_55_7_1 (Handbook III.3.72); (Z_57,8;1) in Sage DM_57_8_1, 'Given by Julian R. Abel', with G = AdditiveCyclic(57). So divisibility by 3 alone does not rule them out. I found no non-existence result for (Z_n,7;1) with n ∈ {21, 39, 51}.

known_cyclic_or_abelian_DM7_for_n.equivalence: CPro1 defines CFR(r,n) as a Circular Florentine Rectangle. CFR(r,n) is equivalent to a (Z_n,r+1;1) difference matrix [inference from the definitions]. An (n,k,1) difference matrix gives k−1 MOLS(n), as stated in arXiv 2412.00480. So a CFR(6,n) gives 6 MOLS(n).

kill_check.scope: Covers only the sources checked. Not finding a claim does not prove non-existence.
evidence: Sym2026 Table 1 (published 2026-01-31; co-author Abel) and arXiv 2507.23376v2 Table 2 both give 39→5 and 51→5.
Sym2024: the only changes below 500 since the Handbook are n = 14, 18, 35, 48, 54, 60, 63, 96 and 486.

Sym2026 Theorem 5: 'there exists a 2-SOLSSOM(v) except for v ∈ {3, 5} and possibly for v ∈ {15, 21, 33, 39, 45, 51, 65, 87, 123, 135}'. Inference: the authors know no (v,7;1) difference matrix with the order-2 automorphism for these v.
Janiszczak–Staszewski 2019, on their isometry-invariant permutation-code search: 'We investigated almost all cases for 10 ≤ n ≤ 100 … improvements just for n = 35, n = 48, n = 63 and n = 96.'
Keita–Shapiro arXiv 2601.22205v1 (2026-01-29), Table 2 lists 39→5 and 51→5. This table is representative examples, not a best-bounds table.
Sage develop: MOLS_table gives 5 for both; only 6-row difference matrices DM_39_6_1 and DM_51_6_1 exist. Sage lags the literature (it shows N(35)=5 and N(48)=8), so its absence alone proves nothing.
Dinitz 'New Results' Part III (2019) and Part VI (2019): nothing for 21, 39, 51 or circular Florentine arrays.
The Abel–Janiszczak–Staszewski Des. Codes Cryptogr. 2025 paper covers only 54, 96, 108 and the n=45 fix.
arXiv API scan on 2026-10-19: the 40 newest of 105 'orthogonal latin squares' abstracts, and all 11 math.CO 'difference matrices' abstracts (newest from 2023). Nothing relevant.
OpenAlex forward citations: Sym2024 has 1 citing work (a GDD paper); the 2025 Des. Codes Cryptogr. paper has 0; Abel–Ge 2005 has 6 since 2015, none about 7-row difference matrices judging by title.
Web searches for six MOLS of order 39 or 51, N(39), Zenodo, and Chinese-language sources: no hits.

context_N21.open_route: CFR(6,21), equivalent to a (Z_21,7;1) difference matrix, is a CPro1-listed open instance that CPro1 did not solve. A construction would also raise N(21) to 6, above the current table value.
context_N21.caveat: CPro1's list of open CFR instances is unreliable. It lists CFR(4,33) as open, but the (Z_33,6;1) difference matrix in Handbook III.3.56 (Sage DM_33_6_1) already gives CFR(5,33) [inference]. Prior attempts: Janiszczak–Staszewski found 5 MOLS(21) as a single orbit under a group of order 105, with no improvement.

key_facts: N(39)≥5 and N(51)≥5 are unchanged since the 2007 Handbook, as of 2026-01-31.
6 MOLS of either order would improve the table.
For 51, any 7-row difference matrix is necessarily cyclic, i.e. a CFR(6,51).
7-row cyclic difference matrices are known for 35 and 55, and an 8-row one for 57.
No 7-row difference matrix is known for 21, 33, 39 or 51.
